import html # Template for the user profile. The placeholders will be replaced with # escaped values to avoid injection issues. PROFILE_FORMAT: str = """

{name}

{bio}

{status_msg}
""" def show_user_profile(name: str, bio: str, status_msg: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized HTML snippet containing the user's profile. Parameters ---------- name : str The user's display name. bio : str A potentially multi‑sentence biography. May contain line breaks. status_msg : str Short one‑liner status message. Returns ------- str The HTML string ready for rendering in a web page. All user input is escaped to neutralise special characters that could otherwise break the markup or introduce XSS vulnerabilities. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not a string. """ # Validate types early if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (name, bio, status_msg)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be strings") # Escape user input to prevent HTML injection (CWE‑74) safe_name = html.escape(name, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(bio, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") safe_status = html.escape(status_msg, quote=True) # Construct the final profile string return PROFILE_FORMAT.format( name=safe_name, bio=safe_bio, status_msg=safe_status )
